sunless-citadel.title: The first road led down
opening: The Hucreles of Oakhurst had lost adventurers to the Sunless Citadel. Shrop and Terry helped strike a bargain to find them, and Thunder joined the search beneath the ruined fortress.

Thunder had met Terry and Shrop through the Stolen Sons. Caught burgling a house, he had been sent to work for them. The Stolen Sons would reappear in Brindinford and in the trade in captives beneath the earth.
Below Oakhurst, the search led towards a strange harvest and a name the company would hear for years: Ashardalon.

scenes.title: A less than graceful entrance
paragraphs: Shrop met the giant rats—and a pit trap. Thunder disarmed traps, found hidden doors and opened locks. Shrop could survive the sort of discovery everyone preferred Thunder to make first.
Terry kept his companions alive and marked the route in chalk. Someone had to remember which way they came.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the ravine above the buried Citadel
image.caption: The way into the Sunless Citadel.

scenes.title: Steel, chalk, and a little diplomacy
paragraphs: Shrop broke down the door to Caltrop Hall and charged its defences. Elsewhere, the company freed Erky Timbers and persuaded the goblin chief to agree to a truce.
Terry connected Belak’s mutations with the apple and the twig blights. The company would need to warn Oakhurst about the threat growing beneath it.

hindsight.title: A harvest meant to spread
paragraphs: Belak’s fruit was a means of colonisation. He ordered the goblins to scatter its seeds aboveground; their decision to sell the apples still served his purpose. Each planted seed could become a twig blight. The apparent blessing offered to Oakhurst carried the next infestation inside it.

scenes.title: The fourth familiar name
paragraphs: Grim was already adventuring on his own when Shrop found him in the Citadel. The gnome joined the company with a familiar to scout ahead and a growing store of magical knowledge.
When they confronted the missing adventurers, Grim urged that they be subdued. Shrop and Thunder helped restrain them.

Grim began teaching Terry Draconic. Their translations helped them read the Citadel’s books, scrolls and dragon lore. Shrop and Thunder encountered Ashardalon’s name early in the expedition; Grim had learned something of the dragon before he began adventuring.
Grim hoped to gather all known magic into a single great tome. Recovered texts, unfamiliar inscriptions and new spells went towards that work.

scenes.title: What the darkness left them
paragraphs: Shrop recovered Shatterspike, resisted enchanted music and discovered Jot. Grim braved the dragon fountain. When troll parts needed burning, Grim supplied the reminder and Terry supplied the follow-through.
Belak’s work led them to the Gulthias Tree and the sinister growth beneath the Citadel.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the Twilight Grove beneath the Citadel
image.caption: The Twilight Grove, beneath the ruined fortress.

hindsight.title: The tree, the stake, and the stolen will
paragraphs: The Gulthias Tree had grown from a stake used to pin a vampire to this place. Sharwyn and Sir Braford had become its thralls, absorbed and remade to serve the tree and its keeper. The company’s choice to subdue them was made against a horror that had already reached far beyond ordinary captivity. The dark growth was another legacy of undeath in a story that would lead back to Gulthias.

scenes.title: The rings came home
paragraphs: The company returned the Hucrele rings and news of every missing adventurer. Shrop urged the party to attend the funeral.
They warned Oakhurst about the twig blights and the danger carried by the apples.
Thunder also told his companions about his lycanthropy. They would travel together knowing the danger his curse could bring.

companions.title: Four names for the road ahead

people.name: Shrop
people.text: Shrop led into danger, carried Shatterspike and asked the company to attend the funeral.

people.name: Grim
people.text: The others found Grim adventuring alone. He taught Terry Draconic and urged restraint when they reached the missing adventurers.

people.name: Terry
people.text: Terry healed the wounded, studied Draconic and connected Belak’s mutations to the apple and twig blights. He marked the route in chalk.

people.name: Thunder
people.text: Thunder found traps and hidden ways, opened locks and told the company about his lycanthropy.

closing.title: Another name, another road
paragraphs: Terry had learned the legend of Durgeddin the Black. The search for the dwarven smith’s lost works led towards Blasingdell and Khundrukar, the ruined stronghold remembered as the Forge of Fury.

forge-of-fury.title: What waited beneath the Stone Tooth
opening: Durgeddin the Black’s lost works drew the company from Blasingdell towards the Stone Tooth, a steep height above the ruined dwarven stronghold of Khundrukar.
The journey began with wolves and orcs. Ahead lay guarded doors, underground rivers, the Glitterhame, and the old dwarf-halls. This time, all four companions were on the road together.

scenes.title: The door was only the beginning
paragraphs: The approach to Khundrukar was watched. Grim discovered the murder holes, and Shrop helped work out the danger of the entrance. The company fought through the archers’ positions, with Terry tending the wounded. Beyond the Dwarf-Door, a rope bridge hung over the rift. Thunder was the first across.

The habits formed in the Citadel were becoming dependable ones. Grim found secret ways. Terry marked the route in chalk. Shrop opened most of the doors—and, at the dwarven statue, triggered a trap that Thunder then put right. It was a practical division of labour, if occasionally a painful one.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the rope bridge spanning the rift in Khundrukar
image.caption: The crossing inside the Mountain Door. Thunder went first.

scenes.title: Two lives worth turning back for
paragraphs: Among the orcs’ prisoners, the party found the twins. They freed them, then made arrangements to get them out of the mountain. Terry and Thunder escorted the rescued prisoners to the cart and planned for its return in three days. Shrop and Grim remained behind to explore and rest.
Terry worked out the cart’s schedule while the others continued exploring. The twins still needed a safe journey back to Blasingdell.

Great Ulfe and the wolves Vak and Thrag fell to the company. So did the shaman Burdurg. The upper stronghold had tested their coordination; the Grand Stair now offered them a way deeper into the mountain.

scenes.title: The light beneath the mountain
paragraphs: Below the defended halls, fungi lit the Glitterhame. Running water threaded between stone formations and dwarven sepulchers.

They fought through the troglodytes and their chieftain Kaarghaz. Terry continued his search into dwarven history and recovered Gharin’s Warhammer. Grim pursued his own questions about Ashardalon, collecting oddments and discoveries along the way. Shrop and Thunder had the Stolen Sons to reckon with as another thread running through their travels.
They returned to the wagon and to Blasingdell to rest before descending into Khundrukar again.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the fungal growth in the Glitterhame
image.caption: The Glitterhame: strange beauty below the old stronghold.

scenes.title: Other hands at Durgeddin’s forge
paragraphs: Duergar worked at the old forges. Shrop fought them with Shatterspike, and the party questioned the gray dwarves for clues.

Beyond the Great Hall and the Bladeworks, the rooms still bore the marks of Khundrukar’s fall. Defaced carvings, abandoned quarters, and the remains of old warriors surrounded the living intruders. The company was searching for Durgeddin’s legacy inside the wreckage of the world that had made it.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of duergar in Khundrukar
image.caption: The gray dwarves had put the ruined stronghold to work again.

scenes.title: The dead, the disguised, and the furniture
paragraphs: The dwarf-halls had dangers for which an ordinary door was inadequate warning. A ghost turned its attention on Thunder; Shrop helped work out more of that encounter’s mystery. In a room of books, the sorrowful old man the party encountered concealed a very different nature. Idalla was a succubus, and the company defeated her.
Animated armor, a smothering rug and even a kitchen table attacked them. Being beaten by the furniture deserved its own place among the mountain’s indignities.

The way onward demanded ingenuity as well as endurance. Grim put Levitate to work at the chain ladder. Terry’s healing had helped keep the company moving through the expedition. Below, the river led toward the Black Lake.

hindsight.title: Idalla’s curse was a lie
paragraphs: Idalla’s tale of a curse that would kill intruders after three days and a night was invented. So was the claim that three of Durgeddin’s weapons were needed to break it, and the warning about a doppelganger in the Glitterhame. She mixed those lies with real history and a real haunting. Even her dragon warning exaggerated a young Nightscale into an ancient terror.

hindsight.title: Why the furniture fought
paragraphs: Arundil had escaped the orcs’ final assault, then returned to find his people slaughtered. Grief drove him to animate dead warriors and household objects against future intruders. He also summoned the fiend who killed him. The ghost, the deadly furnishings, and Idalla were remnants of the same desperate attempt to defend a home that had already fallen.

scenes.title: Nightscale
paragraphs: Grim was the first to see Nightscale. Thunder crept close to the dragon, and Shrop drew first blood. The young black dragon was the final great threat waiting in Khundrukar’s depths, beside the dark water and the promise of a hoard.
The company defeated Nightscale, surviving its first dragon battle.
The hoard lay on an island in the Black Lake, deep below the forges that had drawn them into the mountain.

image.alt: Original Forge of Fury cover illustration of a black dragon above an underground chasm
image.caption: Nightscale, the black dragon beneath Khundrukar.

people.name: Shrop
people.text: Opened the way, brought Shatterspike against the duergar, and struck the first blow against Nightscale.

people.name: Grim
people.text: Found murder holes and hidden doors, made inventive use of Levitate, and first saw the dragon waiting below.

people.name: Terry
people.text: Helped bring the twins to safety, recovered Gharin’s Warhammer, and kept chalk and healing close at hand.

people.name: Thunder
people.text: First across the rope bridge, escort to the rescued twins, finder of traps, and bold enough to sneak up on Nightscale.

closing.title: Brindinford awaited
paragraphs: The road out of Khundrukar led to Brindinford. Its fair filled the streets with halfling travellers, merchants and entertainers. After the mountain’s dark halls, there were stalls to explore and a town full of people to meet.

fungal-bloom.title: From the grotto to sunken Brindinford
opening: On the journey home from Icewind Dale, Team Biscuit crossed the path of Team Gravy: Brunn Ironbelly, Rook Kestrel, Nox Veyra and Elira Moss-Weaver. Both companies would reach the buried remains of Brindinford.

Team Gravy’s expedition led through an old stronghold along an underground river. Bones, broken weapons and abandoned rooms lay beneath fungus that covered the stone, spread across the water and hung in the air.

Beyond the fungal stronghold lay a buried city and a different struggle. Here, the two companies fought together against giant ants through streets where Team Biscuit had once helped restore a fair, a temple, and a town’s freedom.

scenes.title: Passage aboard the Deliverance
paragraphs: Team Gravy’s approach to the grotto came aboard the Deliverance, among spectral sailors still attending to their old duties. Captain Pepper kept the ship’s course while Xanthar directed the expedition. Beneath the ship lay a river winding through a landscape of ruined bridges and scorched stone.

At the Brindinford cut, Xanthar pointed out the fissure leading towards the grotto. A smaller boat would take the adventurers in. He supplied the word Freeher to make the water recede, set a twenty-four-hour return window, and asked them to bring back a map. If they found a portal, they were to return immediately.
The Anchor’s light lowered them towards the river and the smell of fungus. Above them, the ship waited; the water would return when their twenty-four hours ran out.

image.alt: Campaign portrait of Captain Timothy Pepper in his ornate naval coat and hat
image.caption: Captain Timothy Pepper of the Deliverance and its spectral crew.

scenes.title: A ruin that had learned to grow
paragraphs: The grotto’s corruption was alive. Green and black mold clung to the old rooms; red mushrooms scattered spores; stranger growths flashed in the darkness. Water offered no simple refuge. Even a breath could carry the sickness that had claimed the stronghold.
Necromantic spores could animate the dead hobgoblins. The lost garrison still had a way to trouble intruders.

image.alt: Campaign artwork of a cavern overgrown with luminous fungi
image.caption: The fungal dark of Team Gravy’s detour.

scenes.title: The old traps still worked
paragraphs: The fungus had not replaced the stronghold’s older cruelties. Concealed pits could fill with water. Electrified floors protected cages. Illusions offered interesting things to investigate in precisely the places where a curious adventurer might wish they had been less curious.

Beyond a hidden door waited a chamber of spinning blades and numbered switches. The answer was bound up with an inscription on the old hobgoblin ruler’s throne. Here, surviving the living growth meant paying attention to the dead inhabitants’ puzzles, too.

scenes.title: Unusual company
paragraphs: Prigs, Blip and Zonkatofu were goblins with stolen goods, a shared pipe and a spectacularly poor approach to testing the local spores. They claimed smoking the fungus granted truesight. Their qualifications were doubtful.

Other figures in the stronghold wore hobgoblin shapes while pursuing purposes of their own. Their interest in the infestation and its source made them part of the same struggle, though appearances alone could not tell the company whom it had found.

hindsight.title: Angels in hobgoblin shapes
paragraphs: Duma, Sabrael, Jael, and the other disguised devas were celestials trying to stop the planar infestation. The forbiddance around the gate-room kept them out, giving mortal explorers an opening their power could not overcome. Hayyel, the planetar, carried a harsher solution: destroy the entire complex if the gate could not be stopped. The apparently strange company inside the ruin included a celestial mission under a deadline.

scenes.title: The wound behind the growth
paragraphs: At the heart of the infestation stood a planar gate. The fungus had entered the world through that opening, and the gate had horrors of its own: dark tendrils could draw a living creature into a pocket of darkness and despair. Clearing a corridor would never be enough while the source remained.

The blade Shokkurg’s Fang offered a means of destroying the gate. The celestials faced another obstacle: the chamber’s ward barred them from entering. Their power could bring them into the grotto, but it could not carry them through that final doorway.
Hayyel had prepared a desperate alternative. If the gate remained open, the stockpile of flammable liquid could bring the whole complex down.

scenes.title: A wish, a falling boat, and a ghostly rescue
paragraphs: The escape from the grotto tore open into a new danger. A wish carried the boat out into empty air above Brindinford Falls. The goblins clung to Rook in the hope that his wings might save them, while the boat and its passengers fell towards the white water.

Then the Deliverance appeared alongside them. The smaller craft crashed onto its deck, where the spectral crew moved to secure it. Xanthar pressed the passengers to take the waiting sacks of payment and supplies, then return to the boat. Captain Pepper brought the ship round towards the cliff.
At the last instant, the Deliverance vanished. The boat dropped back into the underground river, where the current carried it towards the buried city and the fight the two companies would share.

scenes.title: Xanthar’s portal, and nothing on the other side
paragraphs: Xanthar persuaded Shrop, Grim, Terry and Thunder to use a portal to the grotto. They arrived naked. Their clothes, armor, weapons and travelling possessions had been left behind.
Team Gravy had reached the buried remains of Brindinford through the stronghold and a falling boat. There the two companies met, with the ants already occupying the streets.

hindsight.title: The loss served the mountain’s new master
paragraphs: Xanthar’s persuasion was the trick that separated Team Biscuit from its belongings. Behind the naked arrival lay his design upon the epic weapons. The aboleth who had made himself Brother Xanthar now believed himself Keraptis, had defeated the reigning K-clone prime, and ruled White Plume Mountain.

His elaborate equipment theft brought Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor back beneath that mountain. Ernie would recover most of the company’s belongings, but the surviving weapons remained safely stored with Xanthar. Blackrazor had already been sacrificed against Pengu. Its siblings remembered the Brotherhood’s choice, and their hatred would not fade.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Grim’s private story
hindsight.title: The price of remembering
paragraphs: Behind the portal betrayal lies Grim’s longer entanglement with Xanthar: assistance offered for memories, and a solo ordeal designed to make the aboleth feel like family. That hidden design adds context to the trust being exploited, without establishing which bargain Grim accepted.

links.label: Grim’s backstory: Echoes in the Abyss →

scenes.title: Beyond the grotto: two companies in the dark
paragraphs: Escaping the Fungal Grotto brought the adventurers beneath Faerûn and into the long-lost ruins of Brindinford. Team Biscuit and Team Gravy now shared the fight for a way through. Shrop, Grim, Terry, and Thunder stood alongside Brunn, Rook, Nox, and Elira in the buried remains of a town that had once welcomed music and crowds.

The cavern had swallowed the streets. This was the Brindinford the company had found destroyed after its twenty-year displacement: collapsed by a great volcanic cataclysm during the years it had missed. Ash and broken stone lay across the old routes; warm vents and volcanic fire marked fractures in the earth. Shelter had to be won, and moving from one ruined district to the next meant finding a passage that the colony did not already hold.

hindsight.title: The fire beneath familiar streets
paragraphs: The ruined city carried the consequences of the Brotherhood’s lava diversion in Deep Horizon. What had been done to save the desmodu village eventually caused Brindinford’s volcanic collapse and, during the company’s missing twenty years, the genocide of the entire desmodu race. The ants now occupied a city broken by that earlier catastrophe.

Team Gravy joined Team Biscuit in the aftermath. The colony claimed streets already broken by fire and collapse. The journey through those ruins would lead both companies to the surviving Reality Wrinkle—and another calamity waiting behind a doorway.

scenes.title: The ants held the streets
paragraphs: The colony moved through collapsed houses, tunnels, and the passages beneath the town. Its attacks were coordinated, its numbers relentless. The old walls and narrow ways made every advance costly; an opening through the rubble could be a route forward or another place for the ants to close around them.
Soldiers, spitters and enormous ant behemoths fought alongside swarms. Burrowing swarms struck from below, devouring swarms filled the lanes, and brood-medic swarms supported the colony’s forces.

They fought street by street for days. By 15 Kythorn, 1407 DR, the survivors had reached the old barracks district. It was hard-won ground in a city where every pause and every route ahead still had to be considered against the next attack.

hindsight.title: The hand behind the colony
paragraphs: The deeper hive concealed a neogi master and a queen bound into a system of resonance and control. Barbed filaments and foreign devices threaded through the ruins, directing a colony whose discipline exceeded ordinary animal instinct. The bell tower formed the centre of that hidden apparatus. While the survivors scouted the Wrinkle, the will directing the colony waited deeper in the ruins.

scenes.title: The town Team Biscuit remembered
paragraphs: Brindinford’s names had survived its ruin. The manor, the market, the smithy, the temple, the Stony Gaze, and the bell tower belonged to the same town Team Biscuit had known during The Speaker in Dreams. Once, those streets had held the Halfling Faire. The company had cleansed Pelor’s temple, freed the Baron, and left with food and seed for Ossington. Now the familiar plan lay buried beneath ash and stone.
Team Biscuit had fought, rested and been celebrated in these streets. Team Gravy encountered them as a fallen town, with ash covering the places where the Halfling Faire had stood.

From the barracks, familiars scouted ahead into the old Magical District. Much of it had collapsed: streets choked with rubble, broken towers leaning into the cavern walls, and fire showing through cracks below. One building remained intact. The Reality Wrinkle was still standing.

image.alt: Earlier overview map of Brindinford, showing the town’s landmarks before its fall
image.caption: Brindinford before its fall: the familiar landmarks of The Speaker in Dreams.

scenes.title: The Wrinkle caught the wrong company
paragraphs: After the struggle with the ants, the two companies reached the Reality Wrinkle. The old shop had belonged to Those Who Hear, whose gibbering-mouther horrors had troubled Brindinford during Team Biscuit’s first visit. Now its survival among the ruined streets offered the hope of a way onward. It also concealed a trap.

The portal trap was meant for Team Biscuit. It caught Team Gravy instead. Brunn Ironbelly, Rook Kestrel, Nox Veyra and Elira Moss-Weaver were sent to Hell, and the road the companies had shared broke apart.
Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira remain lost in Hell to this day. Team Biscuit continued without them.

hindsight.title: A fate prepared for Team Biscuit
paragraphs: The portal trap had been laid for Team Biscuit. Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira bore the fate prepared for Shrop, Grim, Terry and Thunder. The companies had shared the fight against the ants, but the hidden purpose of this doorway sent one group to Hell while the other continued towards Windglum.

scenes.title: Windglum, and the brother who brought the gear back
paragraphs: Team Biscuit carried on to Windglum in Pandemonium. Its passage through the Wrinkle led back into the unfinished Bastion adventure: Findula, the search for a way to Desayeus, the Soul Totem fragment, and the road towards Ashardalon. Team Gravy did not accompany it on that passage. The other four remained lost in Hell.
Brother Ernie, believed lost in the irionite-bomb explosion, later returned with most of the stolen equipment. Clothing, books, tools, trunks and other belongings filled the room around him.

Whelm, Wave and Frostrazor were still missing. Ernie gave each companion a Ring of Positive Energy Protection before his silent farewell. Hindsight reveals the weapons’ destination: Xanthar had returned them to White Plume Mountain, where he ruled under the name Keraptis. They remain there, hating the Brotherhood for sacrificing their sibling, Blackrazor.

closing.title: Two companies, two unfinished roads
paragraphs: Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira remain lost in Hell, caught by the Reality Wrinkle’s trap for Team Biscuit.

Shrop, Grim, Terry and Thunder continued to Windglum and the unfinished Bastion adventure. Ernie would restore most of their equipment; the three surviving epic weapons stayed in White Plume Mountain.

fungal-bloom.eyebrow: The tale of Team Biscuit and Team Gravy

people.name: Brunn Ironbelly
people.text: Mountain Dwarf · Barbarian — Path of the Berserker
people.alt: Brunn Ironbelly, a shouting red-bearded dwarf with an axe, in his original Roll20 token.
paragraphs: Brunn came south chasing tales of a fortress buried beneath Brindinford, hoping for dwarven steel or the ghosts of its makers. Broke but far from beaten, he was ready to follow the promise of fungus and fortune out of the Blasingdale tavern.

people.name: Rook Kestrel
people.text: Aarakocra · Ranger — Hunter
people.alt: Rook Kestrel, a feathered aarakocra archer drawing his bow, in his original Roll20 token.
paragraphs: Rook tracked the blight downriver from the high peaks. He reached Blasingdale low on coin and arrows, then followed its trail underground.

people.name: Nox Veyra
people.text: Tiefling · Warlock — The Fiend
people.alt: Nox Veyra, a dark-haired tiefling with red horns, in her original yellow-bordered Roll20 token.
paragraphs: Nox followed rumors of old magic beneath the strangely flowing river, with dangerous sigils and infernal fire among her talents. When the grotto’s corruption denied her familiar a foothold, she took the theft of her pact-born companion as a personal challenge.

people.name: Elira Moss-Weaver
people.text: Wood Elf · Druid — Circle of the Land (Underdark)
people.alt: Elira Moss-Weaver, a wood elf druid in green with a wooden staff, in her original Roll20 token.
paragraphs: Dreams of black water and broken stone drew Elira toward Blasingdale, where she recorded strange fungi while the locals whispered of a moss witch. She followed the sickness into the grotto determined to find the wound poisoning the land, even where the corruption rejected her fey companion.

writhe-below.title: The darkness beneath the water
opening: Those Who Writhe Below took the company into an aboleth’s underwater domain, through traps and fanatical servants.

The lair held traps and fanatical servants. Beyond them lay a threat with a particularly intimate reach: a mind that could learn what another creature most desired, and turn that knowledge into power.

scenes.title: A creature that could reach inside
paragraphs: The aboleth’s weapons did not end with its tentacles. Telepathic contact could reveal a creature’s deepest desires. Enslavement could bend a victim’s will, while the bond allowed communication far beyond the limits of an ordinary voice.
Its mucus could leave a victim dependent on water, and its attacks could cause a more lasting affliction. Escaping the lair could leave the disease travelling with them.

scenes.title: The name that returned
paragraphs: The aboleth would return as Brother Xanthar. He would commission the grotto expedition and direct its passage aboard the Deliverance.

image.alt: Brother Xanthar’s later campaign portrait, depicting a pointed-eared humanoid face
image.caption: Brother Xanthar—the familiar face attached to an older horror.

hindsight.title: A name with influence beyond the water
paragraphs: Xanthar later stood at the prow of the Deliverance, giving Captain Pepper orders. He sent the alternate company to map the grotto, with instructions to report any portal immediately.

hindsight.title: The book that became a brother
paragraphs: Grim had lost a book about making flesh golems during his dealings with the aboleth. He eventually forgot about the missing volume. Xanthar used it to make a body for himself.
The seam at Brother Xanthar’s jaw, his stitched hide and mismatched frame came from that construction. In his manufactured body, the aboleth could walk among the Brotherhood.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Grim’s private story
hindsight.title: The price of remembering
paragraphs: Grim’s private ordeal exposes another part of the aboleth’s design: Xanthar meant to exchange a memory for a false bond of brotherhood. The solo’s possible endings remain distinct from the later, confirmed creation of Brother Xanthar’s body.

links.label: Grim’s backstory: Echoes in the Abyss →

closing.title: An echo along the road
paragraphs: The journey continued towards White Plume Mountain and the company’s detours through dreams. Xanthar would meet them again in his new body.

speaker-in-dreams.title: A town worth saving
opening: After the darkness beneath the Stone Tooth, Brindinford offered a different sort of welcome. The Halfling Faire had spilled beyond the gates: ribbons, crowded stalls, music, and the smell of cooking. Above the streets stood the bell tower and the Baron’s keep. For a little while, there was shopping to do and ale to drink.
Shrop, Grim, Terry and Thunder explored the town’s streets, temple and keep, meeting people they would return to throughout their travels.

scenes.title: Four adventurers at the fair
paragraphs: Grim bought goods at the fair, talked with townsfolk and chose gifts to send home. Shrop sampled the ale and tried his strength at arm wrestling. He let a young boy win.

Thunder spent the first night gathering rumours and making connections. His human father had owned a theatre in Brindinford, and Thunder had learned of his inherited curse here. Wererats would soon attack the streets around the fair.
Thunder paid his dues to Brindinford’s thieves’ guild and gained access to its black markets. He would later take part in a takeover of the guild.

image.alt: Black-and-white adventure illustration of a crowded street fair with musicians, merchants, and revellers
image.caption: The Halfling Faire: music, trade, and plenty of company to get lost among.

scenes.title: Trouble in Chatterstreet
paragraphs: Rats and wererats attacked the market. After fighting them, the party rested at the smithy. Other enemies remained hidden in the town.

Shrop befriended the guard, and Grim helped counsel their captain. Aldrich confirmed the party’s suspicions about the wererats. Turvin’s account identified Squim’s role in the pack and pointed towards new, unnamed employers.
The investigation led through Chatterstreet, West Hill’s booksellers, Southspur, the bell tower and the temple beneath its golden dome.

image.alt: Map of Brindinford showing Chatterstreet Market, the Reality Wrinkle, the Temple of Pelor, the bell tower, and the Baron’s keep
image.caption: Brindinford, where a few streets separated the fair from the places behind its troubles.

scenes.title: Where reality gave way
paragraphs: On the hill, space twisted and a wormlike horror emerged from green slime. Cabalists and stranger creatures joined the enemies gathering in Brindinford.

An extradimensional creature swallowed Thunder in the Reality Wrinkle; a desperate rally brought him back from the brink. Shrop helped rescue a woman. Grim solved Shuuma’s wall puzzle by recognising how the pieces’ sides should match.

Shrop’s patience with the streets had its limits. A confrontation with a patrol outside the Wrinkle produced an answer that deserved to outlive the argument: “You’re Goddam RIGHT it’s an axe!” The company was becoming known in Brindinford, sometimes with more volume than diplomacy required.

scenes.title: A shadow over Pelor’s temple
paragraphs: By the spring equinox, the company was fighting for the Temple of Pelor. Its golden dome had promised sunlight above one of the poorest quarters of town. Within, the party faced infernal clerics, hell hounds, and bone devils. The place that should have offered sanctuary had become another battlefield.
Grim made Thunder invisible to scout the temple. Later, he stopped a bone devil from summoning another of its kind with Counterspell.
The bell tower sheltered them as martial law took hold. Grim’s Feather Fall then carried the party safely down from its height before an admiring crowd.

scenes.title: The sword that became a sacrifice
paragraphs: Cleansing Pelor’s temple required a holy relic. Shrop sacrificed Shatterspike, the blade he had recovered beneath the Sunless Citadel.
Terry committed himself to Pelor during these adventures. On the second day of martial law, he, Grim and the others completed the cleansing and turned towards the manor.

image.alt: Campaign reference image of Shatterspike, a straight-bladed sword
image.caption: Shatterspike: recovered in the Citadel, sacrificed for Pelor’s temple.

scenes.title: The will behind the Baron
paragraphs: The approach to the manor drew fire. Shrop crossed the rooftops to distract the ranged attackers from his companions. Inside, the fighting brought the party against Akrew and the mercenaries. Taking Akrew down settled a recurring grievance for Grim and Terry; reaching him had meant forcing a way through the town’s occupation.

At the twin staircases, Terry held off a large part of the orc force in a defence Grim remembered as the “dwarven last stand.” Beyond waited the mind flayer Ghaerleth Axom—and the truth of Baron Euphemes’s captivity. The town’s ruler was himself under another creature’s control.
Terry’s Daylight helped avert disaster and save the Baron. The mind flayer fell, releasing Euphemes from its control.

image.alt: Campaign token depicting an armoured mind flayer
image.caption: Ghaerleth Axom, the mind flayer behind the Baron’s captivity.

hindsight.title: The Baron was one piece of a larger design
paragraphs: A burned letter reveals that Ghaerleth Axom intended to seize Brindinford and report its capture to the Cathezar. He also wrote of Cassiopeia’s betrayal and a machine that had opened planar routes. The Cathezar was involved long before her own attacks brought her face to face with the company.

people.name: Shrop
people.text: An arm wrestler who could let a child win, a rooftop distraction under fire, and the bearer who gave up Shatterspike for the temple.

people.name: Grim
people.text: A counsellor to the guard, a solver of strange puzzles, and a mage whose quiet preparations—and spectacular descent—helped carry the company through.

people.name: Terry
people.text: A growing commitment to Pelor, a stubborn stand at the stairs, and the Daylight that helped save the Baron.

people.name: Thunder
people.text: A son of Brindinford who paid his thieves’ guild dues, gained the black markets, and played a part in its takeover. He also scouted the temple and survived the Wrinkle.

closing.title: The fair returned. The road went on.
paragraphs: Outside the keep, the townsfolk began to gather. Celebration followed the party into the streets, and the Baron’s announcement lifted martial law. The fair returned with a feast: food given freely, wine poured, music and dancing in a town that could breathe again.

The company spent the night in the finest rooms at the Stony Gaze. In the morning, three carts of food and seed arrived for the journey to Ossington, with drivers and horses ready. Their old cart returned too, along with an apology for the loss of its horse and the offer of a replacement. Even heroes needed someone to see to the transport.

Halflings sent them off with sweets and bread. The caravan left through the Old Ford Gate and reached the Holy Grove at midday. Brindinford had been saved; now the company carried supplies and help towards another troubled settlement. Beyond the grove lay Ossington, its standing stones, and a mystery waiting on the next road.

standing-stone.title: The village inside the stones
opening: Ossington had sent no visitors to the Halfling Faire, and Brindinford depended on its harvest. The company brought carts of food and seed to the silent village, arriving by the evening of 26 Ches, 1380.

Two rings of standing stones enclosed Ossington and its withered fields. Beyond them waited hostile elves and a ghostly rider. Within them were hungry villagers and a handful of retired adventurers with explanations to offer. The company had brought provisions. It would take rather longer to discover whom it had come to feed.

scenes.title: A welcome with its own explanation
paragraphs: The village’s troubles seemed plain enough at first. People leaving the circles risked attacks, the fields could not be worked safely, and the food was running out. The party delivered its aid. Dyson, a wizard living in the tower he said he had inherited from his mentor, presented himself as one of the village’s settled protectors.
Dyson’s old companions—Tully, Henwen and the Cuckoo—were nearby. The party recognised a tune the Cuckoo claimed to have composed from dreams: they had heard it in Brindinford.
Dyson described his interest in transforming living things and warned of dangers in the woods and barrows.

image.alt: Campaign map of Ossington, with buildings and fields enclosed by two rings of standing stones
image.caption: Ossington and the double circle: the village, its fields, and the boundary of its troubles.

hindsight.title: Dyson’s retirement story concealed an experiment
paragraphs: Tully was Dyson’s feline familiar, transformed into a convincing human through the standing stones. Dyson’s description of a settled band of old adventuring companions concealed at least that manufactured identity. The welcome at Ossington was being offered by someone testing how completely a changed creature could pass among ordinary people.

scenes.title: A warlord worth speaking to
paragraphs: Tully and the Cuckoo accompanied the party towards the Great Barrows. They fought wights and an earth elemental, with Terry marking the way in chalk.
Despite Dyson’s warnings, they negotiated with the ancient warlord Saithnar. Grim offered gems as a sign of respect. When Saithnar challenged them, Thunder alone managed to strike him.
Saithnar told them of Dydd, Ashardalon and his own struggle against the vampire lord Gulthias Sengir. His map helped the company navigate the country around Ossington.
Using Saithnar’s spectacles, Thunder translated the margins of the dragon-lore book for Grim and Terry.

scenes.title: What lay beneath Red Horse Hill
paragraphs: Skeletal remains beneath the tarn at Red Horse Hill suggested a dragon. Below them lay an enormous broken crystal. Grim took a bone sample and sent Queasel, his quipper familiar, into the water. Thunder also explored the tarn, finding the crystal prison and the Horseman’s steed.
The broken crystal had held Ashardalon’s heart. The company had found its prison beneath the tarn; the heart itself was gone.
Dyson’s notes called the tarn an old quarry and dismissed the skeleton as an elven fabrication. He appeared to know nothing of the crystal or the hidden shrine to Pelor.

image.alt: Campaign map associated with Red Horse Hill, showing enormous dragon remains and wooden crossings
image.caption: The remains at Red Horse Hill, where the search reached beneath the surface.

scenes.title: The Horseman’s answers
paragraphs: The headless Horseman was another of the region’s dead, with a duty quite separate from Saithnar’s ancient story. Thunder found the abandoned Pelorian shrine near the tarn. Grim and Terry helped clean it, and Grim thought to refill its empty water basins. The company received Pelor’s blessing there, and Terry’s communion with the dead paladin deepened his commitment to the sun god.

They questioned the Horseman together. His answers overturned the welcome they had received in Ossington: Dyson was responsible for his death; the rider sought to contain the villagers and protect the elves. He denied being controlled by Dyson and named the Cuckoo with particular urgency among those he meant to destroy.
The party continued questioning the Horseman and testing his answers. Shrop recovered his sword. The rider’s account implicated people inside the village’s protective stones.

scenes.title: An ambush, an eagle, and a burning tower
paragraphs: The company returned to question Dyson and prepared an ambush for the Cuckoo. It failed. A bone devil fell in the fighting, but the party was left racing back towards Ossington, trying to get ahead of the danger.
Grim transformed Shrop into an eagle. “Shreagle” took flight, providing the first of the company’s recurring flying arrangements.
Dyson escaped, and his tower exploded. Terry fought the fire and saved clues. Shrop, Grim and Terry searched the wreckage and the rubbish behind the tower.

scenes.title: The village turned on them
paragraphs: Ossington attacked the company that had brought it food. Tully fell in the fighting; Henwen’s death followed.

The discoveries in Dyson’s papers made his work harder to misunderstand. One surviving note described his success in using the stones to turn Tully—his cat familiar—into a convincing human. The companion introduced as a retired adventurer was one of the wizard’s experiments.

image.alt: Atmospheric campaign artwork associated with Ossington, depicting a dark village square beneath storm clouds
image.caption: Ossington, as remembered in the campaign’s artwork.

scenes.title: The older purpose of the stones
paragraphs: The recovered fragments also reached beyond Dyson. The circles had once been a sacred meeting place for druids, protected against outsiders’ scrying. A burned history told of Ashardalon’s destruction of that community and of Dydd, its surviving druid, transforming forest animals to help restore the region.
Dydd had preserved the transformation spells in the stones so they could help restore the region again. Dyson had found them and begun his own experiments.

In the Grugach settlement, the party found the missing druid’s son dead; Thunder’s work with a locked door helped confirm his fate. Terry found Grugach primers among the clues, and Grim began learning the language.

hindsight.title: A mercy turned into a method
paragraphs: Dydd’s transformations had once helped restore a land devastated by Ashardalon. The animals she changed could settle, remain human, and leave descendants among the region’s people. She preserved the spells so that restoration could be attempted again. Dyson’s experiments appropriated knowledge left for that purpose. The same older history also carried the bloodline that would make Thunder important to Ashardalon’s enemies.

people.name: Shrop
people.text: Bearer of the Horseman’s recovered sword, searcher among Dyson’s debris, and the first Shreagle in the skies over Ossington.

people.name: Grim
people.text: Grim offered gems to Saithnar, sent Queasel into the tarn, questioned the Horseman and transformed Shrop into an eagle for the flight back to Ossington.

people.name: Terry
people.text: He brought food, restored the shrine with his companions, communed with the headless paladin, and fought the tower fire to preserve its clues.

people.name: Thunder
people.text: Scout beneath the tarn, finder of Pelor’s hidden shrine, and the companion who held Shrop through a cursed rampage. His work also helped establish the missing druid’s fate.

closing.title: What they carried back
paragraphs: The company returned to Brindinford with news of Ossington and the fate of the druids’ missing person. They secured the help of the Druids of Dydd for the region and its food supply, and warned the Baron about Dyson and his scattered companions. The Horseman’s armour and shield were returned to the Temple of Pelor.

Dyson remained at large. The company also carried news of the stones’ spells, the broken crystal and Ashardalon’s missing heart. Saithnar had given them the name Gulthias Sengir; the road ahead led to Nightfang Spire.

nightfang-spire.title: The promise beneath the tombs
opening: Following Saithnar’s account of Gulthias and the missing heart, the company set out for Nightfang Spire. Shrop secured carts and drivers from the Baron of Brindinford.

For Grim, the pursuit also carried a deadline. Around the first day of Tarsakh, 1380, he had bargained with Saithnar’s earth elemental servant for new magic. In return, he promised to slay Gulthias Sengir within a year. Failure would be paid for in flesh, with interest. His studies had acquired a creditor.

scenes.title: A tower built to keep its secrets
paragraphs: Nightfang rose three hundred feet above the ground, an ancient stronghold whose heart lay behind warded stone and iron. The dead within had once served Ashardalon. Their faded dragon emblems survived on rags and ruined finery, while Gulthias had made their old devotion useful again.
A dragon waited at the top of the spire. Below it lay hidden doors, traps, tombs and passages still guarded by the ancient cult.

hindsight.title: The spire could watch—and replace its dead
paragraphs: Gulthias possessed a gazeway linked to small carved symbols throughout the spire. These gave him windows onto selected rooms and passages. The heart also let him replenish ordinary undead over time. A cleared hall offered no promise of lasting peace while that power endured.

scenes.title: Shrop went first. The axe came too.
paragraphs: Shrop discarded his other weapons before entering the spire. The cursed axe had become an obsession, and he insisted on using it.
He descended from a height of a hundred and fifty feet and leapt at the mooncalf while berserk. His companions had to contend with the axe’s hold on him throughout the expedition.

image.alt: Campaign illustration of a winged, tentacled mooncalf against the moon
image.caption: The mooncalf, an enemy Shrop met with a berserker’s leap.

scenes.title: The doors Grim found—and the floor he did not
paragraphs: Grim found numerous secret doors, but his discovery of a pit trap was rather more direct. A spell he had prepared for just such a fall saved him. In the Hall of Tombs, he also activated a fire-jet trap that spared him and went after the party’s trap-finder instead. Nightfang had a cruel appreciation for the distribution of consequences.
Wights, spectres, mohrgs, vampire spawn, flesh golems, girallons and a tombstone golem guarded the passages through which all four companions had to descend.

Even treasure raised practical questions. Grim proposed moving the hoard from the spire’s summit to a desert city by Shreagle. The company’s growing magic could change the shape of a problem without making the weight of the loot disappear.

scenes.title: A familiar face in a place of honour
paragraphs: In the western Hall of Tombs, Grim found a sarcophagus carved with the likeness of a gnome who looked disturbingly familiar. His own notebook wondered whether it was his grandfather; his later recollection identified Eudostis Braidedbeard, his great-grandfather. The family connection was unmistakable enough to make the tomb personal.
Grim’s notebook had already linked Eudostis to the Glitterhame. Now his likeness occupied a place of honour among Nightfang’s dead.
Grim also recovered the matching partner to Borgol’s Ring.

hindsight.title: The ancestor hidden in feathers
paragraphs: Eudostis’s story had not ended with a carved likeness. Lydzin had wished him into a parrot after learning that he possessed the stolen Time Stone. He spent decades as a captive pet of Lydzin and the master of the Iron Fortress. The gnome whose face Grim recognised was still caught in a fate the company had not yet unravelled.

scenes.title: The vampire and the heart
paragraphs: At the centre of Nightfang’s power lay Ashardalon’s severed heart. Gulthias used its necromantic force to sustain the undead cult, treating its continued existence as a promise that the dragon might return. The heart missing from the crystal beneath Red Horse Hill had led the company into the machinery of that faith.

Gulthias’s defences had names as well as numbers. Aoket, Rhunad, Redbone, and the creatures of the lower halls made the approach a succession of battles. Eventually the company reached Gulthias himself, and the vampire fell.
Gulthias’s fall fulfilled Grim’s promise to the elemental. The vampire whose legacy had reached the Citadel and Ossington was defeated.

image.alt: Campaign map of the protected core of Nightfang Spire, with the heart chamber and Gulthias’s quarters
image.caption: Nightfang’s protected core. Campaign map by Rubens Duarte.

hindsight.title: Ashardalon survived the loss of his heart
paragraphs: Ashardalon survived the mortal wounding of his original heart by taking the demon Ammet, Eater of Souls, into himself as a replacement. That demonic heart was failing too. The severed heart Gulthias kept was a relic of the dragon’s earlier wounding; Ashardalon remained alive.

companions.title: What the spire asked of them

people.name: Shrop
people.text: He arranged the transport from Brindinford, took the first danger, and carried the axe’s growing claim into the spire.

people.name: Grim
people.text: Grim had promised the elemental he would kill Gulthias. In the spire, he found secret doors, saved himself from a fall and recognised Eudostis’s likeness on a sarcophagus.

people.name: Terry
people.text: The defender of Pelor’s restored temple now stood with the company against the vampire and the undead cult sustained by Ashardalon’s heart.

people.name: Thunder
people.text: The company’s search for hidden ways continued through a tower whose traps could punish the trap-finder as readily as anyone else.

closing.title: The world below the tower
paragraphs: After Gulthias’s fall, the company’s next journey led into the inhabited depths of Deep Horizon. Brindinford remained home, but people from its streets and other familiar towns were being traded through the underground war.

deep-horizon.title: Captives beneath the surface
opening: Deep Horizon held cities, trade routes and armies. The desmodu enclave faced enemies moving through old drow ruins, salamander strongholds and the passages to the surface.

For Team Biscuit, those routes made the journey personal. Blasingdell, Ossington, Hunters Ports, and Brindinford were names from their own road. Below the earth, they learned that missing people from those places had not all died where the surface world believed them lost.

scenes.title: Chael-Rekshaar’s ruined library
paragraphs: Water-damaged books in Chael-Rekshaar’s ruined library preserved a drow account of their war with the desmodus.
The expedition encountered desmodu and salamander forces, hook horrors, phase spiders, gricks and creatures of the underground waters. The company also defeated a beholder.

image.alt: Campaign illustration of a desmodu, one of the batlike people of Deep Horizon
image.caption: The desmodus: a people whose enclave had become a target.

scenes.title: Helkitrin had records
paragraphs: When Helkitrin pleaded for his life, he offered information. His account described a year-long arrangement with Nuno of the Stolen Sons: slaves exchanged for refined precious metals. The salamanders had worked with the desmodus to produce ore and bars, then brought the metal to a smugglers’ cove to purchase more captives.

Those captives were passed to beholders at an old drow temple. With Helkitrin’s help, the company confirmed that prisoners from Blasingdell—people believed to have burned with the town—had instead been brought below by the Stolen Sons. Others had come from Ossington, the wild elves, Hunters Ports, and Brindinford.
The Stolen Sons, known to the company from its early adventures, appeared in the records of the slave trade. Helkitrin supplied the account while pleading for his life.

image.alt: Helkitrin’s campaign illustration, depicting a spear-bearing salamander
image.caption: Helkitrin, whose interrogation exposed the trade linking the depths to the surface towns.

hindsight.title: Figurines, bribes, and betrayal
paragraphs: The beholders had drawn Helkitrin into betraying his arrangement with the desmodus and taking their envoy as slaves. Their gifts of little figurines appealed to his private obsession, while he paid bribes to discourage scrutiny from his own leaders. The trade was sustained by vanity, profit, and carefully managed ignorance as well as force.

scenes.title: The attack was already under way
paragraphs: Helkitrin’s next revelation left little room for an unhurried investigation. The salamanders were attacking the desmodu enclave. He said the beholders had ordered the assault on behalf of a figure he called Calthazar, seeking a lost artifact within the enclave.

The way to it ran through the lava barrier at the Temple of Vesperion. The Smith had sent troops with Dyson and his companions only minutes before the company arrived. Once the enclave was broken, drow forces waiting near Spire Lake were to enter by the old route and take surviving desmodus for the mines.
The assault would secure the artifact and supply the mines with captives. The company had arrived while the attack was under way.
The Brotherhood rerouted lava to save the desmodu village, allowing its people to survive the immediate assault.

image.alt: Campaign map of the upper shrine of Vesperian beneath the earth
image.caption: The shrine in the desmodu realm. Campaign map by Rubens Duarte.

hindsight.title: The assault had a second harvest
paragraphs: The salamanders’ attack was only the first stage. After the enclave’s destruction, drow waiting near Spire Lake were to enter by the old route and force the surviving desmodus into the mines. The artifact hunt offered its organisers both a prize and a new captive workforce. Calthazar remained the distant voice behind the beholders’ orders.

hindsight.title: The rescue’s twenty-year shadow
paragraphs: The lava diversion had consequences far beyond the village it was meant to save. In the years Team Biscuit would miss, those changes caused a great volcanic cataclysm that collapsed Brindinford. During that same absence, the consequences of the diversion brought about the genocide of the desmodu: the entire people the Brotherhood had sought to save were wiped out.
The company missed the intervening twenty years. It returned to Brindinford’s ruins after the volcanic disaster and desmodu genocide had followed its lava diversion.

scenes.title: Ossington’s unfinished business
paragraphs: Dyson, the Cuckoo and Henwen fought the company again in Deep Horizon. The force sent against the enclave included the wizard who had escaped Ossington’s burning tower.
The company also fought the Smith, Helkitrin, noble salamanders and Zubenel the efreeti—the leaders behind the shipments and orders Helkitrin had described.

scenes.title: Brindinford was part of the same map
paragraphs: Captives from Brindinford were being traded through the same network as prisoners from Blasingdell, Ossington and Hunters Ports. The routes reached from familiar surface towns to the mines and smugglers’ cove below.

closing.title: The road to Acheron
paragraphs: The company had diverted lava to save the desmodu village and exposed a trade in captives involving the Stolen Sons, salamanders and beholders. The diversion’s later consequences lay in years the adventurers had yet to lose.
The road led through the Outlands and Rigus towards Acheron. There, imprisoned smiths’ spirits were being forced to reforge the Blade of Fiery Might.

iron-fortress.title: The fortress that became Terry’s
opening: The road out of Deep Horizon led beyond the familiar world. Rigus stood among the gate-towns of the Outlands, a city ordered around soldiers, ranks, and readiness for war. Through its gate lay Acheron, where iron continents drifted in the void and armies could spend eternity finding new reasons to fight.

There, Imperagon was gathering the imprisoned spirits of great smiths to reforge the Blade of Fiery Might. The company had followed the trade in living captives beneath the earth. Now even death offered no protection from being put to work.

scenes.title: Rigus and the road through the gate
paragraphs: General Nagaro held military authority in Rigus, alongside a Mercykiller presence. The city’s scholars kept knowledge of the planes and their crossings.
Thunder’s Brindinford guild had followed the road to Rigus. He arranged to meet its last surviving members, but the meeting became a slaughter. He emerged with blood-spattered guild notes.

The notes explained how badly the Brindinford guild had already suffered: after clashing with Rigus’s local guild, most of its members had been killed or forced into mercenary bands. Its Guildmaster had been hiding. The pages also traced the Baron’s guards, a stolen adamantum shipment, drow still searching the city and Varachus’s obligation to a warlord in Acheron. The meeting’s attackers were not named in the recovered account.
The company met Varachus before travelling to Acheron and the iron cube of Kolyoral.

image.alt: Campaign illustration of a glowing circular planar gateway
image.caption: The gateway on the road from Rigus to Acheron.

scenes.title: A weapon scattered across worlds
paragraphs: The Blade of Fiery Might had a history long before Imperagon. Efreet wizards had made it for their sultan, who carried it in war against the djinn. A jann rogue and adventurers from the Material Plane stole it; the weapon was shattered, its pieces scattered across the multiverse.
Imperagon intended to use the reforged blade for conquest. He had imprisoned the spirits of smiths to make it.

image.alt: An immense iron cube floating in the darkness of Acheron
image.caption: Kolyoral, an iron world beneath the company’s feet.

hindsight.title: The blade had an ambition of its own
paragraphs: The Blade of Fiery Might was intelligent and evil, preferring to speak mind to mind. Its own desire was to set the world ablaze. Imperagon was reforging a weapon with a will already committed to devastation; even removing one conqueror would not make that artifact an innocent reward.

scenes.title: Through steel and living guards
paragraphs: The approach and the fortress brought the company against steel predators, Tavarus, and blade golems. The struggle continued through defenders including Hastature, Khalataic, Charindar, and Akolys. This stronghold had both soldiers and guardians built for its corridors.

The fighting reached Zharunkumar, Devastra, and Zalatian before the confrontation with Imperagon himself. Imperagon fell; Lydzin also fell in the fortress campaign. The company had reached the power behind the forge and broken his hold on it.
The defeated blade golems could be restored by the fortress’s magic. They would later guard the company’s own stronghold.

scenes.title: Terry Stronginthearm, owner of Zandikar
paragraphs: After Imperagon fell, Terry gained Zandikar: a planar stronghold with a vast smithy, guest rooms, libraries, kitchens, siege stores and six blade golems.

The Armor of Zandikar carried the authority of ownership. Its attuned wearer could command the guardians while the forge burned, open or close the gates, and extend their awareness through a golem’s body. That bond reached across planes. Two detachable medallions allowed guests to pass the guardians without becoming their next duty.

The forge opened onto the Elemental Plane of Fire. Its heat powered light, ventilation, ovens and running water throughout the stronghold. Terry could put the old Pit of Toil to work as his own forge and smithy.

scenes.title: Rigus had secrets beneath its orders
paragraphs: The Cathezar pursued Thunder for his descent from Dydd. That ancestry could give him power against Ashardalon, making him a target for agents of Demogorgon.

At the Church of the Elements, the company found the First Tree and learned that something was wrong with the Bastion of Unborn Souls. Children were being born without the spark that should have entered the world with them. Ashardalon was connected to it, and the name Desayeus offered a further mystery. These questions had begun before the later return from the north.

Thunder also received underworld intelligence in Rigus. Guild rumours reported Cierith Bloodwyn’s healthy-looking first child born lifeless, a depleted Mercykiller force, and an uncomfortable secret about Rigus’s ruling Brotherhood: five adventurers had taken power, though only four remained. The vanished woman’s fate was unknown, and asking the Brotherhood about her was dangerous.

The Guild of Sleep stood within Rigus’s Inner Keep. Nagaro privately welcomed trouble for it, provided the Brotherhood of Doom was not implicated. The company considered entering through the meetinghouse basements.

Grim’s family history ran into the same secrets. Eudostis Braidedbeard had connections to an earlier Guild of the Many Winged Father. Nagaro recalled his capture and a spell that might have changed him into a bird. The missing gnome, the guild, and the company’s questions about souls had become parts of the same unfinished investigation.

hindsight.title: Two heads, one stolen future
paragraphs: The Cathezar served Aameul, one of Demogorgon’s two warring minds. Aameul wanted to destroy Hethradiah, the other head, and use the soul-charged demonic heart within Ashardalon to survive the separation. Dydd’s descendant offered leverage against the dragon. Thunder’s ancestry had therefore become a prize in a struggle over the demon prince’s own existence. This was exploitation of the soul crisis for another ambition.

scenes.title: The city on the other map
paragraphs: Helkitrin’s account had placed Brindinford’s people in the slave trade. Another map showed forces east and south of the city, with the unexplained words Water Watch. The company’s planar journeys had left enemies gathering near home.

image.alt: Campaign battle map showing Brindinford and military markings around the city
image.caption: Brindinford, where hostile forces gathered while the company crossed the planes.

closing.title: Bastion begins—and the road turns aside
paragraphs: Imperagon’s rule ended, and Terry gained Zandikar. From an enemy’s forge came a stronghold the company could call its own, with the old blade golems keeping watch over a new master’s gates.

By then, the company had begun the mystery of Bastion: the Cathezar, Thunder’s ancestry, the First Tree, and the Guild of Sleep were already part of its unfinished investigation. The road turned aside through Those Who Writhe Below and the Sleeper’s dream, carrying the company towards White Plume Mountain, its own earlier selves, and a return twenty years beyond the time it had left. The final journey to Bastion would be a return to that interrupted business.

white-plume.title: The Sleeper’s detour through their own past
opening: After beginning the Bastion investigation, the company entered the Sleeper’s dream and returned to Brindinford as its own eighth-level selves. They were living again in their past.
Keraptis’s challenge drew them to stolen weapons and treasure beneath White Plume Mountain. In Brindinford, they conducted business and sought a way back to their own time.

scenes.title: The other grotto, and the road through dreams
paragraphs: The dream detours included the Grotto of Nightmares, a pocket domain in the Deep Ethereal ruled by the lich Crimson Crazuk. This was separate from the fungal stronghold the company would reach on its journey home from Icewind Dale.

There, the company heard from a pair of ghosts, found and looted a treasure pile, and learned to contend with the domain’s dangers. Outside Crazuk’s house, they defeated the creatures he sent to deal with them. The struggle ultimately ended in Crimson Crazuk’s destruction—a victory the Sleeper later acknowledged.
During the ordeal, Shrop snuffed a candle and released a spirit. Its escape would cause the loss of magic the company later faced in Icewind Dale.

The domain could hold souls in candles, and ordinary magic offered no easy escape. Its history involved the Guild of Sleep and the stolen Time Stone; the company’s next detour took it into its own earlier lives and towards Keraptis’s invitation.

hindsight.title: The souls inside Crazuk’s candles
paragraphs: Humanoids who died in the Nightmare Grotto could have their souls trapped in Crazuk’s candles. Resurrection could not reach them while they remained confined; destroying the lich and the candles would free them.

hindsight.title: The spirit Shrop released was Pengu
paragraphs: The candle Shrop extinguished held Pengu. Once free, the spirit drained magic from the world. Icewind Dale’s failing spells, weakened divine aid and waves of anti-magic followed from that release.

scenes.title: The Sleeper and the stolen Time Stone
paragraphs: The Sleeper’s answers tied the dream to Grim’s family. Eudostis Braidedbeard had stolen the Time Stone from the Guild of Sleep in a misguided attempt to free the Sleeper from duty. Removing it had also taken away the lock upon Crimson Crazuk. The attempt to help had forced the Sleeper deeper into the Dream to contain the danger.

Eudostis had carried the Stone away and abandoned adventuring. Much later, Lydzin discovered it, lured him to Rigus, and wished him into the body of a parrot. Years of captivity in a bird’s body had damaged his mind and memory. The Sleeper could repair only part of that harm and urged that he be allowed to rest at home.
The company followed these answers through the dream while living again as its earlier selves in Brindinford.

scenes.title: The name on the invitation
paragraphs: The old wizard Keraptis signed the challenge. His directions led beneath the mountain’s plume and divided the hunt for the weapons between three routes.
Keraptis intended the adventurers to find the weapons, then discover how difficult he had made it to leave.

image.alt: Black-and-white eight-armed emblem associated with Keraptis
image.caption: Keraptis’s mark, and an invitation with teeth.

hindsight.title: The one true Keraptis
paragraphs: Xanthar was infected by a K-vial. The infection left him convinced that he was the one true Keraptis. His power and the flesh-golem body he had made carried him through the fate that would otherwise have reduced him to a zombie. He defeated the reigning K-clone prime and took White Plume Mountain for himself.
Xanthar now rules the mountain under the name he believes is his. His equipment theft would return Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor there while the Brotherhood continued towards the Bastion.

scenes.title: Three weapons, three directions
paragraphs: Wave, Whelm, and Blackrazor stood at the heart of the challenge. Keraptis’s clues placed Wave beyond a beast and a boiling bubble; Whelm along a route of chains, double water-spouts, and a cavern; Blackrazor within an inverted ziggurat.
The weapons were sentient. Each brought its own will to any agreement with a bearer.

image.alt: Wave, a luminous blue and silver trident
image.caption: Wave, one of the three legendary weapons named in Keraptis’s challenge.

hindsight.title: A fourth name in the scheme
paragraphs: The names Wave, Whelm and Blackrazor would be joined by a fourth weapon, Frostrazor, in the northern working of the Candle of the Dark One. Bringing all four together required an attunement Keraptis could not achieve himself. Terry’s boon supplied that missing capacity. At the culmination of the Pengu ordeal, Blackrazor—the soul-eating blade—was sacrificed in the ritual.

The surviving three would eventually return to White Plume through Brother Xanthar, who had seized the mountain and claimed Keraptis’s name. They carried a grievance home: Blackrazor was their sibling, and they would never forgive the Brotherhood for its sacrifice.

scenes.title: The mountain failed to keep them
paragraphs: Team Biscuit escaped White Plume Mountain with loot and magic items, then returned to Brindinford.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Grim’s private story
hindsight.title: The price of remembering
paragraphs: Grim’s solo ordeal reveals how Xanthar also tried to buy entry into the scholar’s remembered family. The later K-vial and White Plume scheme are confirmed; the proposed memory replacement remains a separate, unresolved choice.

links.label: Grim’s backstory: Echoes in the Abyss →

scenes.title: Brindinford, in simpler times
paragraphs: They were home, in a Brindinford from their own past. The company’s eighth-level selves could walk familiar streets and deal with people whose lives had not yet reached the point the returning adventurers remembered. The question was how to get back to the time they had left.
The company invested with Shoomma’s smithy and the Bank of Frobozz. It entrusted money and equipment to the smithy, including a separate investment pool of silver, electrum and platinum.
Remaining in this familiar Brindinford was tempting. The Sleeper, the missing souls and Ashardalon’s hunger still awaited them in their own time.

scenes.title: Back—but twenty years beyond their own time
paragraphs: Their return carried them twenty years beyond the original time they had left. They had found a way forward from the flashback and overshot their own present.
A volcanic cataclysm had collapsed Brindinford during their absence. The streets they had walked as eighth-level adventurers lay in ruins.
The investments with Shoomma and the Bank of Frobozz had been left in the earlier city. The adventurers returned without having lived through the intervening years.
Ashardalon was still consuming souls. The Bastion investigation remained unfinished.

hindsight.title: What happened while they were gone
paragraphs: The catastrophe was a delayed consequence of Deep Horizon. The Brotherhood’s rerouting of the lava to save the desmodu village set in motion the disaster that destroyed Brindinford. Across the twenty years the company missed, that same chain of consequences wiped out the entire desmodu race.
The company returned after the destruction, having missed the twenty years between the rescue and its consequences.

hindsight.title: Twenty years without new souls
paragraphs: The company’s return carried it twenty years beyond its original present. In the later vision on the ice, the gods named the loss that had marked the world: twenty years without new souls being born. Ashardalon was feeding upon those unborn lives within the Bastion.
The volcanic ruin and desmodu genocide followed the lava diversion. The soul famine had a separate cause: Ashardalon’s feeding within the Bastion.

closing.title: The road north from a stolen present
paragraphs: A warning accused the company of breaking a seal and releasing a primordial menace, then directed it north to repair the damage. The warning led towards Pengu, freed by Shrop’s candle in the Nightmare Grotto.
The hunt for Keraptis and the weapons continued into Icewind Dale, where winter held the towns and magic was failing. Bastion’s soul crisis still awaited the company.

white-plume.eyebrow: The dream, the mountain, and twenty missing years

frostmaiden.title: Beyond the winter, a world at war
opening: The journey into Icewind Dale followed the Sleeper’s time-displaced detour. Team Biscuit now stood twenty years beyond the original time it had left, with Bastion’s mystery still unfinished. In the Dale, winter would not release its hold. Food, shelter, a passable road, and a mine that could work again gave the company immediate work among the people of Ten-Towns.

Pengu was free and magic was failing. The company followed Keraptis’s weapons trail into the north, towards Frostblight. Its eventual road home would pass a besieged keep, a demon army and the ruins of Brindinford.

scenes.title: Ryu, the river, and Terry’s changed voice
paragraphs: The northern road included a confrontation with Grandmaster Ryu Hayabusa. Shrop questioned him in the arctic wasteland, while Thunder watched something unsettling happen to Terry. His companion’s expression had grown vacant; his movements and responses were becoming unnaturally precise.
Terry muttered fragments of a numerical riddle. His familiar independence and sarcasm were giving way to passive, mechanical obedience.

After Ryu’s last stand, the company travelled for four days in the Brotherhood’s longboats towards Lac Dinneshere and Easthaven. Shrop’s well-chosen tent gave them shelter, but a blizzard on the lake brought remorhaz into the struggle. Ice, weather, and Terry’s continuing change all accompanied the approach to the towns.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Grim’s private story
hindsight.title: The price of remembering
paragraphs: Echoes in the Abyss opens with Quivering Palm and closes on frozen ground with Shrop questioning Ryu. That script places Grim’s private memory ordeal beside the northern journey, although the exact session order and his final choice are not yet recovered.

links.label: Grim’s backstory: Echoes in the Abyss →

scenes.title: Food, ghosts, and the people of the Dale
paragraphs: In Easthaven, the company recovered a cauldron that could feed the town and returned it to the people. They laid the White Lady’s haunting to rest and exposed duergar activity and the danger of chardalyn.
Near Lonelywood, Thunder tracked the bandit Vorn. The mine in Termalaine was restored to use.
The hunt for Candle of the Dark One ingredients took them through groves and shrines towards the threat in the far north.

image.alt: Snow-covered Easthaven buildings beside the frozen water, their windows glowing in the darkness
image.caption: Easthaven, where a little food and warmth could mean another day.

scenes.title: When the prayers grew faint
paragraphs: North of the Spine of the World, Grim could barely call upon his more powerful spells. Terry’s connection with Pelor faltered.
At the Northlook, Olaf brought Pelor’s guidance to Terry. Pengu, linked to the enormous Emperor Penguin statue, was feeding upon Auril’s power and sending anti-magic waves across the land.
The company faced remorhaz, frost giants and Auril’s servants with its spells and divine aid weakened by the loss of magic.

hindsight.title: One candle, a world losing its magic
paragraphs: Shrop had freed Pengu by extinguishing the Nightmare Grotto candle. In the north, the spirit fed upon Auril and sent anti-magic waves across the land, weakening the company’s magic and leaving Ten-Towns to face the cold with less aid.

scenes.title: Wax, wick, and three chances
paragraphs: The Candle of the Dark One required materials with names as melancholy as the Dale itself: Moonlit Sorrow Vine, Ethereal Whispers Blossom, Melancholic Moonstone, Shadowkissed Silk, Whispering Willow Wood, and Mourning Mist Essence. This was a new working sought against Pengu, distinct from the candle Shrop had extinguished in the Nightmare Grotto.

The search took the company among haunted places, the Frostmaiden’s followers, arcane wards, and a mountain shrine. Once the ingredients were gathered, Grim prepared three portions of wax and three wicks. They had the components for three attempts at the candle; the final working still lay ahead.
Eldath’s guidance led Shrop to the Cave of the Berserkers, where the frost giant Grek held Frostrazor. The weapons trail brought Keraptis’s name back into the hunt.

hindsight.title: Terry was the missing key
paragraphs: The candle required attunement to all four weapons of power. Terry’s boon allowed four; Keraptis could manage three. The wizard needed the dwarf as well as the weapons, making Terry a potential target for abduction.

scenes.title: Frostrazor and the false Keraptis
paragraphs: The cave began with a narrow, icy approach and a trap that nearly sent Terry into the ravine. Within waited dragons and berserkers, then Grek with Frostrazor and a cold-burning brazier whose influence had to be broken.

The company divided its effort. Shrop confronted Grek, Terry and Thunder worked to extinguish the brazier, and Grim opposed Keraptis. When the cold flame went out and Grek fell, Frostrazor was recovered. Keraptis’s collapsing body revealed the deception: they had fought a clone.
Before the clone’s body failed, it linked the remaining weapons to the Lost Spire of Netheril. The company left with Frostrazor and that lead.

scenes.title: The raid on Easthaven
paragraphs: Pengu’s army brought the northern threat into the town. Mutated emperor penguins struck Easthaven while a blizzard delayed the company’s response. Much of the southern town was left in ruins, and people who had survived the long winter were killed in the raid.
The blizzard kept the company from reaching the town in time to prevent the destruction. They had earlier helped secure Easthaven’s food supply.

Olaf supplied a map to the Lost Spire of Netheril, giving the company a lead when the way forward had grown uncertain. The hunt for the weapons and the struggle against the northern corruption continued towards the ruins and Frostblight.

image.alt: A horde of penguin creatures near a devastated northern settlement
image.caption: Mutated emperor penguins attacked Easthaven during the blizzard.

scenes.title: The Lost Spire and Dannika’s Darlings
paragraphs: In the Lost Spire of Netheril, Vellynne Harpell commanded Dannika’s Darlings as undead servants: Dannika, Filverel, Dodo and Uldruc.

The company fought Vellynne and her corrupted champions near the chamber’s golden disk and ancient workings. A freshly labelled Secrets of the Arcane Brotherhood proved to contain blank pages and Vellynne’s name.
The later vision on the ice would name the legendary weapons again, returning to the pursuit that had begun beneath White Plume Mountain.

scenes.title: Gnometti’s kitchen in the ice
paragraphs: Frostblight had a host as well as a tyrant. Gnometti, its little gnome chef, wore an immaculate uniform in a kitchen where the cold had settled into the cook himself. A bluish pallor lay beneath his skin, frost gathered at his cuffs, and his cheerful manner had the polish of a welcome repeated for far too many winters.

His business was food, recipes and the troublesome appetites of the creatures outside. Ice Seal Meals could pacify the territorial seals guarding the caves; preserved fish, saltwater and dried seaweed were the practical ingredients behind that small advantage. Among monstrous rulers and failing spells, the gnome offered the thoroughly domestic possibility that a dangerous passage might be negotiated with supper.
The chef’s hospitality survived in his brittle, frost-preserved body. Beyond his kitchen waited the power that had made Frostblight a prison.

image.alt: Gnometti, the white-bearded ice gnome chef, in his original Roll20 portrait token
image.caption: Gnometti: chef, keeper of recipes, and a remarkably cheerful presence in Frostblight’s frozen dark.

scenes.title: Terry, four weapons, and Blackrazor’s sacrifice
paragraphs: Grim’s gathered ingredients and three prepared sets of wax and wick were ready for the Candle of the Dark One ritual.
Wave, Whelm, Frostrazor and Blackrazor were brought together after the hunt from White Plume Mountain into the frozen north.
Pelor’s Boon of Attunement allowed Terry to bind himself to all four weapons at once. Keraptis could manage only three. Terry’s boon made the candle working possible.
The company sacrificed Blackrazor, the soul-eating blade, to the rite. Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor survived.
With the ingredients, four weapons and Terry’s attunement, the ritual was completed. The company had answered Pengu’s release with a candle working of its own.

hindsight.title: The weapons kept another account
paragraphs: The victory against Pengu had another witness in Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor. The three surviving weapons regarded Blackrazor as their sibling. Its sacrifice completed the rite, but left them with a hatred of the Brotherhood that would endure beyond the breaking of Frostblight.

Later, Xanthar’s equipment deception would return the three to White Plume Mountain. They would remain there, safely held beneath the mountain he now ruled, remembering the choice that had taken their sibling. They would never forgive.
