scenes.title: Pengu’s last shape
paragraphs: Frostblight’s final struggle brought the company against the creatures Pengu had remade. Corrupted emperors, Panguini and Dreamkeepers stood along the way. Mad Kaelith fell during the fighting. At the heart of the stronghold waited Pengu, bound upon a throne of jagged ice, black runed chains stretching from her body into the frozen walls.
Pengu was the spirit Shrop had released from the candle. It had weakened the world’s magic, corrupted the northern creatures and turned Auril’s power against the land.

When the final blow landed, Pengu’s great form convulsed and folded inward. Her body compressed until the enormous presence upon the battlefield had become a black egg ten feet tall, gleaming like liquid obsidian. The chamber fell silent around a slow, deliberate heartbeat.

Each pulse drew warmth from the air. Frost crept across the floor, and the egg’s reflective surface returned distorted glimpses of the companions. Pengu’s fighting form had fallen. What remained was a vessel still alive with the power that had filled the stronghold.

Then Frostblight came apart. The monumental penguin statue cracked and shattered; stone and ice fell through the ruin of the frozen citadel. The company’s victory became an escape as the ice shelf broke beneath the way out. They plunged into the arctic sea and survived upon an isolated iceberg, with sheer ice above the water and no land in sight.
The company survived on the iceberg after completing the ritual and defeating Pengu. The first promise of magic’s recovery would come in a dream.

image.alt: A huge penguin monument beneath the aurora, surrounded by an army in the snow
image.caption: Frostblight’s monument, before the ice and stone gave way.

hindsight.title: Mad Kaelith had once been a queen
paragraphs: Kaelith had been Aeloria Frostsong, the compassionate queen who led the Panguini against Pengu. The invasion broke her resistance and her mind, turning the former defender into Pengu’s enforcer.

hindsight.title: What the egg still held
paragraphs: Pengu’s obsidian egg retained its heartbeat and hunger for warmth after Frostblight fell. Its later fate remains unknown.

scenes.title: A vision on the ice
paragraphs: Pelor, Eldath and Auril appeared together in the company’s dream on the ice. Eldath said magic was beginning to recover after Pengu’s defeat, though it would need time. Auril acknowledged that Pengu had made a prison of her domain.
The gods warned of twenty years without new souls being born. Ashardalon was still consuming unborn lives, even as magic began to recover.
They called the company back towards Rigus to resume the Bastion investigation.

For Thunder, the dream also held the Deliverance and Captain Timothy Pepper. The Pendant of the Ethereal Anchor bound Thunder’s soul to the ghostly ship. Pepper had warned him of its price: dying while wearing it would make Thunder the ship’s captive captain in Pepper’s place. In the vision, the ship endured and searched for him; that reassurance did not remove the bargain.
Beneath the ice, Angajuk the great whale offered passage onward towards the planes.

scenes.title: Through the Maw, into Acheron
paragraphs: The way out of the northern waters led towards a strange gateway beneath a sea that had fallen unnaturally still. Ancient runes marked the chasm called the Silent Maw. Beyond the ordeal of the Hungry Maw, the company’s next awakening was aboard a vessel resting on Angajuk’s back, with silver mist surrounding them where the sea should have been.

Angajuk was adrift in the Astral Sea until a distant rhythm gave direction: the sound of forgework reaching through the void. The passage carried them past broken cities, shattered titans, and relics of old wars. Ahead lay a vast iron cube scarred by trenches, with a fortress of red stone at its centre.

The whale would go no farther. Angajuk opened a rift, and the company passed through into gravity, heat, smoke, and iron. They had reached Acheron again. The Red Keep waited below, holding a history of the company’s absence that none of the northern victories had prepared them to meet.

scenes.title: What had happened to Rigus
paragraphs: Father Cuthbert’s Chronicle of the Reclamation described the fall of Rigus. Its wards had failed with the loss of magic, and demons poured through the broken Lion’s Gate. The city fell in less than a week.

Cuthbert also recorded a quieter catastrophe: infants born without souls and resurrection magic faltering. The company had heard of the failing cycle of life before leaving Rigus. The chronicle showed that the danger had endured through the city’s fall and the refugees’ flight. Defeating an army could not, by itself, restore those missing lives.

Cuthbert led survivors towards the Red Keep. There, a relic touched by Pelor’s fire became the heart of the Cold Forge. Those who died defending the Keep could rise again within it. Refugees, warriors, and Formacid allies gathered around that miracle, and the Church of the Reclamation took shape.
Survivors had raised shrines to the adventurers as the Blessed Company, and Terry’s armour had been found waiting. The returning party met a faith that had grown around its absence.

hindsight.title: The hunger behind the silent cradles
paragraphs: Pengu’s anti-magic reached Rigus, disabling its arcane and divine wards and allowing the demons through the Lion’s Gate. Shrop’s release of the spirit had helped leave the city defenceless.

Ashardalon caused the separate soul famine. He consumed unborn souls to feed his failing demonic heart in the Bastion of Unborn Souls. The northern vision named twenty years without new souls. Breaking Pengu’s hold allowed magic to recover while that predation continued.

scenes.title: The Red Keep and the general’s cell
paragraphs: By the time of the return, the Red Keep had endured a prolonged demonic siege. Its defenders held because the walls, the Formacid tunnels, and the Cold Forge gave them a way to resist losses that should have broken them. Father Cuthbert kept the rite alive by faith and memory.

General Nagaro’s arrival brought another wound from Rigus. The former commander came to the Keep injured, under suspicion of having fled before the city’s fall. Placed in protective custody, she was found dead by morning. Her death left an accusation without a settled answer.

Cuthbert recorded the Blessed Company’s return on the fifteenth of Marpenoth, 1406. Survivors who had raised shrines to them greeted living saints; the adventurers faced the siege and Nagaro’s unresolved death.

scenes.title: The demon army
paragraphs: Vrocks, hezrous, glabrezus, chasmes and nalfeshnees fought in the demon army. Its greater horrors included goristros, mariliths and balors.

Alongside them fought Iron Fang veterans, Crimson Scorcher veterans, Spirewatch archers, and Blightspike skirmishers. Beast-handlers brought their own menagerie into the struggle: giant scorpions, a bulette, a shambling mound, and a hydra. This force combined disciplined fighters, monsters, and the strength of the Abyss.
Team Biscuit fought through the army. In the later fighting, it defeated an Ultroloth Ascendant.
Brindinford was still ahead. Before they could call the journey home complete, the company would find another familiar place transformed—and another company already caught in its troubles.

closing.title: Home, beneath the streets
paragraphs: With Pengu defeated, the egg still pulsing and magic beginning to recover, the company survived the war around the Red Keep.
The way home led into Fungus Grotto and sunken Brindinford. Shrop, Grim, Terry and Thunder would fight giant ants alongside Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira among the buried streets.

bastion.title: The road returns to the dragon
opening: The company first learned Ashardalon’s name in the Citadel and followed his dead worshippers through Nightfang Spire. The Cathezar’s pursuit, the First Tree and the Guild of Sleep drew them into the crisis of children born without souls.

Their investigation was interrupted by dreams, a return to their eighth-level lives and a jump twenty years beyond their original time. Icewind Dale, the Red Keep’s war and ruined Brindinford delayed their return.
Pengu’s defeat allowed magic to recover, but the gods’ vision warned that Ashardalon was still consuming unborn souls. Shrop, Grim, Terry and Thunder now sought a way into his refuge.

scenes.title: An old shop, a new world
paragraphs: The Reality Wrinkle had survived where much of Brindinford had fallen. Team Biscuit and Team Gravy had fought through the giant ants of the Sunken City to reach the old Magical District. There, a portal trap intended for Team Biscuit caught Brunn, Rook, Nox and Elira instead. Team Gravy were sent to Hell and remain lost there; Team Biscuit’s onward road led to Windglum.

The crossing delivered Team Biscuit into a cramped storeroom. Brindinford crates, ash-marked trunks, cracked scroll tubes, and old papers crowded the shelves. Much of what the Wrinkle’s mages had once brought here was gone. Outside, the wind screamed through Pandemonium.
In Windglum, the party sheltered beyond the great mirror at the back of the Wrinkle. Pandemonium’s winds screamed outside.

scenes.title: Findula finds the way
paragraphs: Findula waited among the travel chests with a small harp across her lap. The company had helped free the lillend. To repay that debt, she sought Eco, the guardian of Desayeus’s prison.

Windglum offered a pause. Equipment could be replaced, wounds could close, and the crooked stalls could occupy adventurers who had spent too long away from a market. At night, the company returned through the mirror to bedrolls among the crates. Findula came and went, following traces and studying the difficult roads between worlds.
Findula summoned them to a map, candles and a compass with trembling crystal points. She had found Eco, whose location changed daily. The route was open only while the trace held.

scenes.title: The guardian who was the door
paragraphs: Eco stood between the company and Desayeus, the God Who Was Banned. A solar accompanied by the planetar Bramam, she had guarded the prison for centuries. No hidden tunnel or convenient spell could replace her. Her own body could become the gateway.

The company sought permission. Shrop pressed the question of whether Eco could open the way under divine command; Pelor’s answer granted passage to speak with the prisoner, while expressly forbidding his release. They were to enter carefully and leave his chains alone.
Grim approached the audience seeking counsel and help against Ashardalon. He made no claim to be Desayeus’s liberator.

hindsight.title: A life bound into the lock
paragraphs: Eco’s death would open the passage for three days. Her body was the prison’s only living entrance. Even after the gateway opened, the binding would still hold Desayeus and the Faithful inside.

scenes.title: The god who remembered his name
paragraphs: Desayeus waited in a prison worn down by centuries. Broken instruments, ruined art, and the devotion of his remaining Faithful surrounded a being who had once been worshipped. His immense body still carried the bearing of a god. The fractured pendant at his chest carried what remained of his claim.

Grim and Thunder questioned him about the Bastion, the dragon, and the Soul Totem. Desayeus had been divine before he claimed dominion over the unborn. The other gods had stripped him of that divinity and broken the Totem. One fragment remained with him; another had provided Ashardalon with a way into the Bastion.

The company needed the piece he still wore. Its request touched the last remnant of an office he had lost, and the last possession he could hold against his judges. Grim asked to borrow it. Thunder brought the danger back to his own blood, hunted because of Dydd and seeking a way to end the fate that pursued him.

hindsight.title: Why the gods left mortals at the threshold
paragraphs: The Ban of the Unborn forbade divine interference with souls before incarnation. Desayeus’s attempt to claim them had brought the other gods down upon him. Their fear of that same prohibition helped leave the Bastion beyond the aid mortals might expect from prayer. Pelor’s permission concerned Eco’s doorway; it was no promise that a god would enter the Bastion and finish the company’s work.

scenes.title: The price of the fragment
paragraphs: By the time the company prepared to leave, Eco had been defeated and was dead. Desayeus had yielded his Soul Totem fragment, which Thunder carried out of the prison.
Desayeus remained bound. The company returned through Pandemonium to the Wrinkle, with the Positive Energy Plane and the Bastion still ahead.

scenes.title: A debt paid in grief
paragraphs: When the company returned to the hidden room, Findula had gone. Her papers, instruments, and personal belongings had disappeared from among the familiar clutter. A folded note waited at the centre of the table.

Eco was Findula’s sister. In her note, Findula accepted that her own choices had helped bring about Eco’s death, though she had neither raised the blade nor opened the door. She believed stopping Ashardalon justified the cost.
Findula considered her debt settled. She neither expected nor wished to speak with the company again.

image.alt: Findula’s handwritten farewell, grieving Eco and declaring her debt to the party paid
image.caption: Findula’s note ended her alliance with the company after her sister Eco’s death.

scenes.title: The man who had survived the explosion
paragraphs: Brother Ernie stood amid boxes, trunks, bottles, books and recovered property. Weathered and battered, he had survived the irionite-bomb explosion the company believed had killed him.
These were the belongings lost through Xanthar’s grotto portal. Ernie had recovered most of the equipment; Team Gravy remained lost in Hell.

There were questions about Rigus, Father Cuthbert, the Brotherhood, and the Church of Terry. Grim wanted to know how Ernie had survived and how he had crossed the planes. Ernie greeted them with his old broad smile and applied himself to the explanation with gestures and an interpretive dance of magnificent commitment and uncertain informational value.

Whelm, Wave and Frostrazor were still missing. Blackrazor had been sacrificed against Pengu. Ernie’s apologetic chalk drawing showed a short thief carrying the surviving three away; Grim suspected a connection to his relative.

image.alt: Brother Ernie smiling in an upstairs room crowded with recovered trunks, equipment, and belongings
image.caption: Brother Ernie with most of the missing equipment, and an explanation delivered through gestures and interpretive dance.

hindsight.title: Where Ernie’s recovery ended
paragraphs: Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor had been taken back to White Plume Mountain through Brother Xanthar. The equipment deception had served the designs of its new ruler: infected by a K-vial, sustained by his power and his manufactured flesh-golem body, Xanthar had defeated the current K-clone prime and claimed Keraptis’s identity for himself.

Xanthar now keeps the surviving weapons safely beneath White Plume Mountain. That is why they were absent from Ernie’s recovered belongings. The company’s suspicions at the reunion did not uncover their destination.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · The weapons’ viewpoint
hindsight.title: We remember our sibling
paragraphs: We are Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor, back beneath White Plume Mountain. Blackrazor should be here with us.

Brother Xanthar brought us home. He calls himself Keraptis now. The mountain keeps us safely, beyond the Brotherhood’s hands. Ernie could return their clothes, books and travelling gear; we remain here.
We knew Blackrazor’s hunger and its voice. The Brotherhood offered our sibling to the rite that ended Pengu’s dominion, then carried its victory into another adventure.
We hate them for that choice. We will remember our sibling forever. We will never forgive the Brotherhood.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Grim’s private story
hindsight.title: The price of remembering
paragraphs: Grim’s uncertainty about brothers has a darker echo in his solo nightmare: Xanthar intended to plant a trusted older brother in his memories. The script does not establish that it worked, and it supplies no proof that Ernie was Xanthar or knowingly helped him.

links.label: Grim’s backstory: Echoes in the Abyss →

scenes.title: Four rings and a silent farewell
paragraphs: Ernie gave each companion a Ring of Positive Energy Protection for the journey ahead. The Positive Energy Plane could kill an unprotected traveller by filling the body with too much life.
He presented the rings without a speech. There were embraces, and then a departure through the office door. Warm motes of light gathered around the old friend as he faded from sight.
The company kept his rings and recovered property. It still had no explanation for what he was or where he had gone.

image.alt: Brother Ernie walking through a doorway as warm golden motes gather around his cloak
image.caption: Ernie faded into warm motes of light beyond the office door. His destination remained unknown.

scenes.title: Into too much life
paragraphs: With the Soul Totem fragment, the company could follow the road beyond Windglum. The shard served as the focus for their passage and the guide through the brilliance beyond it. Pandemonium’s screaming winds gave way to the white expanse of the Positive Energy Plane.

Here there was no ordinary ground or sky. A traveller chose a direction to become down, then fell through the light. The same energy that closed wounds pressed more life into a mortal body than it could safely contain. Healing and destruction stood dangerously close together.

The fragment drew them towards a vast crystalline form: the Bastion of Unborn Souls, spread across the radiance like an immense snowflake. Somewhere within its branching halls, souls gathered before their first lives. Somewhere deeper, Ashardalon was feeding.

image.alt: Campaign illustration of an immense branching crystal Bastion in the brilliance of the Positive Energy Plane
image.caption: The Bastion of Unborn Souls in the campaign’s travel illustration, its crystal branches spread across the Positive Energy Plane.

scenes.title: The entrance had teeth
paragraphs: Fiends and an enormous spiderlike retriever guarded the Bastion’s entrance.

Glabrezu, a hezrou, and a nalfeshnee joined the fighting. The retriever struck with great claws and rays of destructive magic. Grim’s chain lightning leapt among the attackers while the others fought through the space around the guardian.
After defeating the retriever and fiends, the company used the Soul Totem fragment to pass the sealed portal.

scenes.title: Dragonspawn among the crystal trees
paragraphs: Inside, Po, Krushar, and Thalidorus met the intruders. The defenders brought blades, axes, jaws, and fire into the crystal halls. Po issued challenges across the fighting; Krushar’s two heads and paired weapons made a brutal answer to anyone trying to hold the way.
Grisly, a half-dragon bear, emerged from the crystal grove with fiery breath and heavy claws.

The company broke through. Po fell, followed by Grisly, Krushar, and Thalidorus. Their defeat opened the route deeper into the Bastion. The party searched what the fallen had carried, reclaimed useful protections and weapons, and continued towards the thing at the centre of it all.

image.alt: Campaign portrait of the armoured dragonspawn Po
image.caption: Po, one of the defenders within the Bastion.

scenes.title: Predators in the birthplace of souls
paragraphs: The company destroyed four soulsippers whose attacks drained life from their victims, then pressed deeper into the Bastion.
Farther in, they fought the Cuckoo’s demon guard and Tamion’s ambush. A vrock screeched through the battle, and Tamion’s long whip dragged at its victims.
Terry was driven down in the later fighting. The battered company still had occupied chambers to cross before reaching Ashardalon.

scenes.title: The blood the dragon feared
paragraphs: Thunder had carried the answer to one part of the mystery within him. Dydd, the druid who had mortally wounded Ashardalon’s heart, was his ancestor. That bloodline had drawn the Cathezar’s pursuit and made him useful to powers whose interest in the dragon had nothing to do with saving children.
In Desayeus’s prison, Thunder had named Dydd, claimed their shared blood and called on Ashardalon to feel the pain of his heart’s destruction again.

Shrop had fought his way here without sight. Grim had argued with Desayeus, and Terry had sought Pelor’s permission to enter the prison. All four had brought Dydd’s descendant within reach of the dragon.

scenes.title: What beat inside Ashardalon
paragraphs: Ashardalon had survived his ruined heart by taking Ammet into himself. When that replacement began to fail, he turned to the Bastion’s unborn souls to sustain his life. His feeding left the world outside without new souls.

image.alt: Campaign portrait of Ashardalon, the ancient red dragon
image.caption: Ashardalon, sustained by unborn souls within the Bastion.

hindsight.title: The replacement heart had a name
paragraphs: Ashardalon’s replacement heart was Ammet, Eater of Souls, a demon bound within the dragon. That transplant was failing. Consuming the Bastion’s raw life force sustained Ashardalon and made him dependent upon remaining at its centre. His hoard had become the supply keeping him alive; the lives he consumed were souls that had never reached birth.

The vision after Frostblight had named twenty years without new souls. Pengu’s loss of magic and Ashardalon’s feeding were different calamities: the first could begin to heal while the dragon continued consuming the unborn. Reaching the Bastion meant confronting the hunger that the northern victory had not ended.

hindsight.title: A second predator wanted the prize
paragraphs: Aameul, one of Demogorgon’s two minds, wanted Ammet’s soul strengthened by that stolen life. With it, he hoped to survive the destruction of Hethradiah and exist alone. His agents’ search for Dydd’s descendant was part of that design. A blow against Ashardalon could threaten one monster while serving another, and the demon within the dragon carried a danger of his own.

closing.title: Beyond the last door
paragraphs: The company had reached the Bastion. The confrontation with Ashardalon still lay ahead: the dragon’s fate, Ammet’s release or confinement, and the rescue of the unborn souls remain unresolved.

Other matters await them beyond the dragon: the surviving weapons in White Plume Mountain, Ernie’s departure, Findula’s grief, the investments left across the years and the homes they might return to.

grim-memory.title: The price of remembering
opening: Xanthar offered Grim hints, clues and assistance in exchange for memories. The scholar could gain an answer and forget what he had paid for it.

In the solo adventure the GM remembers, Grim listened to recordings of his past, chose the true recollection and risked losing a memory when he chose wrongly. The surviving script, Echoes in the Abyss, supplies the aboleth’s purpose and several possible endings.
The scenes reconstruct that scenario, with its hidden design labelled Revisionist. Grim’s exact answers, the original audio and the final branch remain unrecovered.

scenes.title: 1. The scholar before the bargain
paragraphs: Before the abyss there were books, a comfortable burrow, and stories of dragons. Hortletott Brightburrow bound and sold books; Deannartie made jewelry. Uncle Theothottle Braidedbeard’s library supplied the kind of treasure Grim could never leave alone.

Theothottle’s grandfather Eudostis had seen a dragon. A great diamond supposedly taken from its hoard glittered through the family story, even while the stone itself remained missing. After decades of reading, Grim went out to seek the answers no book at home could give him.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Hidden design
hindsight.title: The appetite Xanthar chose to feed
paragraphs: Family, dragon lore and the satisfaction of solving a mystery were the foundations of Grim’s identity. Xanthar’s script uses each as an invitation: a welcoming hearth, an ancient text, a hoard, a companion who always seems to know the next answer.

image.alt: Grim’s earlier campaign portrait.
image.caption: The dragon scholar before the long road. Original campaign portrait.

scenes.title: 2. The palm, the fall, and the water
paragraphs: The script opens with a monk’s Quivering Palm striking Grim unconscious. The battlefield falls away. Cold water closes over him, and a pull he cannot resist draws him back into Xanthar’s underwater lair. His own memories shine at a distance, as unreachable as stars.

Memaw’s cottage appears with walls of running water. Old mentors accuse Grim. A cruel double wears his face, and mirrors show triumphant and broken versions of him. Xanthar’s illusions challenge his memory before offering the bargain.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Chronology
hindsight.title: Where this fits on the road
paragraphs: The scripted return places Shrop, Ryu and Grim on frozen ground, connecting the ordeal to the northern journey. Its exact session date and position among the Icewind Dale events remain unconfirmed. It belongs beside that chapter without moving the established adventure order.

scenes.title: 3. Four memories with something wrong
paragraphs: Grim must listen to four recollections and identify the detail Xanthar has changed.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Distorted memory
hindsight.title: Brindinford: lightning where fire should be
paragraphs: One vision has Grim destroy Brindinford with lightning. The script asks whether the remembered magic should have been fire. That discrepancy is the test; the vision supplies no evidence that Grim destroyed the city or caused its later volcanic collapse.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Distorted memory
hindsight.title: The Desmodu: rescue rewritten as slaughter
paragraphs: Another vision makes Grim direct volcanic lava into the Desmodu’s ancestral home. Against it comes the recollection that he diverted the flow away and saved them. Xanthar has turned the meaning of the act inside out, making a rescue feel like guilt.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Fabricated memory
hindsight.title: Rigus: a crime that never happened
paragraphs: The vision places a cursed Manual of Flesh Golems beside Grim while his creation rampages through Rigus. The script explicitly calls this incident fabricated. Xanthar’s later use of Grim’s real lost book to make his body is a separate, confirmed event.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Corrupted gift
hindsight.title: The scroll: knowledge with a parasite inside
paragraphs: A vial and tattered scroll promise a new spell, something to learn and share with friends. Dark veins reveal a living parasite within the apparent gift. The image belongs beside the campaign’s K-vial deception, but this scripted vision does not establish every action Grim actually took with a vial.

scenes.title: 4. Home, with one extra place at the hearth
paragraphs: The burrow is warm again. Hortletott and Deannartie are there, and the illusion gives the younger siblings the names Merrifoot, Pippin and Tansy. Familiar voices, family work and small domestic comforts make the scene feel safe.
Xanthar appears as an older gnome, knowing the stories and the diamond as though he had always been part of the family. Grim is offered a welcome built around that invented familiarity.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Hidden design
hindsight.title: The brother was the intended invention
paragraphs: The GM’s goal was to extract a memory and replace it with the belief that Xanthar was a trusted older brother. Familiarity and shared experiences were meant to establish the bond. Whether Grim accepted it remains unknown.

image.alt: The campaign map of Grim’s home.
image.caption: Campaign artwork of Grim’s home illustrates the setting borrowed by the illusion. No map of the solo dream has been recovered.

scenes.title: 5. The mentor who had always been there
paragraphs: In a forgotten library, Xanthar leads Grim to a hidden alcove and a text full of dragon lore. Their work seems effortless. The aboleth’s guidance mingles with the teachings of Theothottle until a new voice begins to sound like an old part of Grim’s education.

The dream changes to an expedition with Terry, Shrop and Thunder. Xanthar sits among them, recounting dragons and discoveries as shared adventures. His details are convincing. His presence is the flaw: why can Grim remember the journey, but not remember this companion being there?
The final temptations return to a dragon-hide book, a glittering hoard and the family hearth. In each, Xanthar offers the thing Grim wants—and places himself beside it.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Behind the scenes
hindsight.title: A cast assembled to make the illusion persuasive
paragraphs: The scenario also prepares Professor Thistledown, Captain Stormstride, Archmage Nightshade and Elder Stoneheart: scholar, explorer, mysterious magician and guardian. These are supporting figures in the written ordeal, not confirmation that every one appeared in the played solo or in a surviving recording.

scenes.title: 6. How a memory could be lost
paragraphs: The GM recalls recorded voices and choices that could cost Grim a memory. The written scenario adds saving throws to recognise the illusions and resist Xanthar’s influence.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · How the ordeal worked
hindsight.title: The written resistance rules
paragraphs: The script starts Wisdom and Charisma saving throws at DC 15. Succeeding at either can expose an inconsistency or resist the influence. Failing both deepens the entanglement and can permit further manipulation or memory alteration. Success gives a +2 bonus to later checks, with the possibility of lower DCs as resistance grows.

Those are prepared mechanics, not a record of Grim’s rolls. The script’s illustrative roll of 16 is an example. Neither it nor the audio-choice recollection identifies which particular memories Grim lost.

scenes.title: 7. Teeth around the Crystal Nexus
paragraphs: The written nightmare includes a survival trial: waves of Umber Hulks attack a pulsing Crystal Nexus. Grim can draw on the crystal to renew his magic while resisting them.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Unconfirmed encounter
hindsight.title: The prepared Umber Hulk trial
paragraphs: Five waves were scheduled for rounds 3, 5, 7, 9 and 11, with one to three Umber Hulks determined by a die roll. The source does not establish how this encounter played out. No kills, experience awards or spent resources from this preparation have been added to Grim’s statistics or the shared battle record.

scenes.title: 8. The offer, with both endings exposed
paragraphs: When the water stills, Xanthar offers clarity, strength and forbidden knowledge for a small fragment of memory—something he says Grim will hardly miss.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Possible outcome · Acceptance
hindsight.title: If Grim accepted
paragraphs: In the acceptance branch, Grim wakes with an altered memory and a bond to an apparently benevolent presence. This would prepare him to accept Xanthar’s agent as family, fulfilling the older-brother design.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Possible outcome · Resistance
hindsight.title: If Grim resisted
paragraphs: In the rejection branch, Grim keeps his original memories and becomes more determined to resist Xanthar. Doubt and unease can persist after the ordeal.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Unresolved outcome
hindsight.title: The choice still missing from the account
paragraphs: Both endings are published here because they were possibilities. Neither has been selected as the canonical result. The exact audio choices, memories surrendered, assistance received for each payment and final answer remain open for Grim’s player or the GM to restore.

scenes.title: 9. Snow, Shrop, and the wrong familiar face
paragraphs: The scripted closing tears away the water. Grim wakes on frozen ground with his companions nearby. For a moment, Ryu appears to be a fallen friend. Then the scene resolves: Shrop is questioning a bound and battered enemy.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Scripted ending
hindsight.title: A closing written to leave doubt
paragraphs: This is the scenario’s closing scene, not a recovered transcript of the table’s final moments. Its confusion over Ryu echoes Xanthar’s intended manipulation, but does not by itself tell us whether the bargain succeeded.

scenes.title: 10. The brother who acquired a body
paragraphs: Grim’s book on making flesh golems became lost and eventually forgotten. Xanthar used it to manufacture the body in which he walked among the Brotherhood.

Later, the K-vial convinced Xanthar that he was the one true Keraptis. His power and constructed body spared him the zombie fate; he defeated the current K-clone prime and took White Plume Mountain. The grotto portal stripped Team Biscuit of its equipment, and Wave, Whelm and Frostrazor returned to the mountain. Blackrazor had already been sacrificed in the rite against Pengu.

hindsight.label: Revisionist · Xanthar’s deception
hindsight.title: The brother Xanthar wanted Grim to remember
paragraphs: Xanthar used Grim’s missing flesh-golem book to build the body he wore as Brother Xanthar. He also planned to alter Grim’s memories so the gnome would believe they had grown up together, with Xanthar as his trusted older brother.
The nightmare’s family scenes and invented shared adventures were meant to make that lie feel familiar. Whether Grim awoke believing it remains unknown.

image.alt: Brother Xanthar’s campaign portrait.
image.caption: Brother Xanthar, in the body he made using Grim’s missing book.

closing.title: A backstory with missing pages
paragraphs: Xanthar’s design is known. Grim’s final answer remains missing, along with the original recordings and the record of any memories surrendered. His player or the GM may yet restore those details.
